invariance.name: Invariance
invariance.gist: What you may vary without moving the answer. Most laws are this one.

round-trip.name: Round trip
round-trip.template: Render, then parse, and you get the form back. Parse, then render, and you get its normal form.
round-trip.gist: Render then parse is exact; parse then render is exact up to normal form. Nothing is lost on the way out and back.

refinement.name: Refinement
refinement.template: With less in, an answer stays, becomes unknown, or says how much it could not read.
refinement.gist: What a reader missing payloads is promised, and how it is told.

order.name: Order
order.template: Any two distinct things compare one way. With a held safe whole value and a numeric bound, exactly one of at-least and below holds. Present times obey the corresponding time law.
order.gist: Strict total orders and complements: no ties between distinct things, no gaps where the test answers.

exactness.name: Exactness
exactness.template: Where the line is: an if and only if where the law states one, otherwise a guarantee on one side of it. Where the law refuses, it says what it refuses with.
exactness.gist: Each law states its exact boundary: an equivalence, a one-way guarantee or a named refusal.

limit.name: Limit
limit.template: This one moves, or can't be done here, and here is who accounts for it.
limit.gist: What doesn't hold, said as plainly as what does.

questions.arrival: What if records arrive late, out of order, or twice?
questions.current: Which record is current, and what if two disagree?
questions.withheld: What if a reader doesn't hold every payload?
questions.spelling: What if the same thing is written two ways?
questions.tests: What does a test on a record answer?
questions.refused: What is refused, and how is it said?
questions.text: What survives a trip through text and back?

questionNotes.arrival: Twice is different for a count or a sum: delivering records again moves them. That is a limit; where the guarantees stop says who accounts for it.
questionNotes.spelling: These laws cover set order and repeats in about, prev and erases. They cover object member order and calendar-date spellings of the same occurred span. Each accepted instant has one spelling. They also cover test order and batch draft order. They promise no other spelling invariance.

Distinct.says: each id is handed over once

View.says: a view: what a reader holds of a record may lose its payload, and the envelope is untouched

EnvOnly.says: the store's rule for who may replace whom reads only envelopes

Forms.says: the forms of one id agree: the same envelope, and the same payload wherever it is held

Acyclic.says: the batch is acyclic: its labels can be ranked so that a draft uses only labels ranked below its own

OneThing.says: every record names exactly the same single thing

SectionValidity.says: section ids are nonempty and distinct

MatchingSectionIds.says: the parsed ids equal the base ids in order

MemberNames.says: the object's member names are distinct

Meaning.says: an assignment of ids to labels that fits the batch

Newer.says: the content order itself, as the relation compared

Stripped.says: a fraction written without trailing zeros: the moments the reader makes

ParsedInstant.says: the actual instant parser accepts the text and returns these numeric fields

ParsedMoment.says: the actual instant reader accepts the text and returns the stated moment

incremental = batch.question: arrival
incremental = batch.change: whether records are folded in parts or all at once
incremental = batch.scope: Proved for Count and LatestBy. Sum, Min and Max are step folds, for which it holds by construction; folds over heads inherit it from LatestBy's state (heads.late).

count.repeats.question: limits
count.repeats.says: Deliver the whole set twice and each record is counted again: the count doubles. Any record delivered again is counted again. That is why the read path hands each id over once (input.distinct).

latest-by.set.question: arrival
latest-by.set.change: how the records arrive, the set kept
latest-by.set.stays: every thing's state (its heads and winner)
latest-by.set.scope: Within one store an id names one record.

latest-by.order.question: current
latest-by.order.says: The winner is a head: nothing about its thing names it in prev. It is newer than every other head by content order: span, then emitted, then id.

id.digest.question: text
id.digest.says: An id's digest has exactly 32 bytes. Reading these bytes gives the same id. Two ids have the same text only when they are equal.
id.digest.scope: The model keeps every record id and reference below 2<sup>256</sup>. Reading any 32 bytes gives an id below 2<sup>256</sup>. Writing that id back gives the same 32 bytes. The model's SHA-256 returns 32 bytes. With the model's SHA-256, an id written from bytes equals the id written from the number. The model does not derive fold records from these hashes.

base32.canonical.question: text
base32.canonical.says: The base32hex decoder accepts exactly the encoder image. Decoding encoded bytes recovers those bytes. Equal encoded texts have equal bytes.
base32.canonical.scope: The encoder uses lowercase base32hex without padding characters. The decoder rejects nonzero unused bits. The fixed-width reader also requires the stated byte count. These results hold for every finite byte list and text, without a hash assumption.

id.text-order.question: text
id.text-order.says: Actual String lexical order on id text equals numeric digest order.
id.text-order.scope: Both inputs have type RecordId. This type bounds each id below 2^256 and gives each digest exactly 32 bytes. The theorem uses Lean's existing String order, not a separate text-order relation. JS UTF-16 order and Rust byte order agree with Lean String order on ASCII; canonical id text is ASCII by construction.

instant.unique.question: spelling
instant.unique.says: Two accepted instant texts with the same moment are equal.
instant.unique.scope: The premises use the actual instant? parser on each String. The proof derives calendar and clock bounds from successful parsing. It assumes no parser injectivity.

instant.round-trip.question: text
instant.round-trip.says: Parse then render recovers the original accepted instant text, character for character.
instant.round-trip.scope: The premise uses the actual instantParts? parser. The renderer writes its numeric calendar and clock fields and its fraction. It does not retain the input text.

content order.question: current
content order.says: Any two records with different ids order one way: by span, then emitted, then id. Never by how a time is spelled.

latest-by.repeats.question: arrival
latest-by.repeats.change: how many times a record is delivered
latest-by.repeats.scope: Within one store an id names one record.

heads.whole-view.question: current
heads.whole-view.says: Whole-reader heads combine every thing's heads, once per id, in content order.

latest.newest.question: current
latest.newest.says: Latest chooses the newest whole-reader head. Its other heads stay in content order.

latest.one-thing.question: current
latest.one-thing.says: Latest equals the previous global LatestBy state on one-thing input.

numeric.safe-whole.question: tests
numeric.safe-whole.says: Numeric slots read only safe-whole values. Nonwhole numeric payloads count as unread.

sum.perm.question: arrival
sum.perm.scope: The model, JS and Rust use unbounded integer sums. A future bounded port must refuse overflow with sum-overflow, never wrap.

sum.repeats.question: limits
sum.repeats.says: Deliver the whole set twice and each record is added again: the sum doubles. Any record delivered again is added again. That is why the read path hands each id over once (input.distinct).

input.distinct.question: arrival
input.distinct.says: The read path hands each id over once. dedup leaves each id once. Where an id names one record, deduplication keeps the same records.
input.distinct.scope: Only dedup is proved; a fold called directly on a list with repeats counts them.

acc.set.question: arrival
acc.set.change: the order, for any step that commutes

acc.late.question: arrival
acc.late.change: whether a late record, not yet folded, is folded onto the cached state or the whole set refolded

heads.set.question: arrival
heads.set.change: how the records arrive, the set kept
heads.set.stays: any answer worked out from the heads

heads.late.question: arrival
heads.late.change: whether a late record is folded onto the cached heads or the whole set refolded
heads.late.stays: any answer worked out from the new heads

heads.why.question: limits
heads.why.says: Max's scalar state cannot maintain the maximum over changing heads. Folds over heads therefore keep LatestBy's state.

view.no-resurrection.question: withheld
view.no-resurrection.stays: the set of heads, by id
view.no-resurrection.scope: Each head comes back in the view's form. A record superseded within a thing is never current there.

view.refines.question: withheld
view.refines.says: Hide payloads and a where answer stays, or becomes unknown.

result.unread.question: withheld
result.unread.says: A fold does not guess. It counts the records whose test is unknown and the selected records it cannot read.
result.unread.scope: Count can read every selected record. Latest-by counts each head once when its payload tests are unknown, after the source and envelope tests select it. Collect counts each unknown record once, before its limit. It counts heads when it follows replacements, and all records otherwise. Max over heads counts each head whose n field lacks a readable safe whole value. Numeric folds count hidden, missing, nonnumeric, nonwhole and unsafe whole values as unread.

result.full.question: withheld
result.full.says: When every test answers and every covered record is readable to the fold, unread is zero. The result equals the selected fold.
result.full.scope: A payload that is here but lacks the field, or holds it as text, isn't readable to a numeric fold.

select.set.question: arrival
select.set.change: the order the records arrive in
select.set.stays: the split into read and unread
select.set.scope: Each id is handed over once (input.distinct).

settle.set.question: withheld
settle.set.stays: what the reader keeps (one record per id)

settle.keeps.question: withheld
settle.keeps.says: A payload any place holds is kept, unless it is erased.

settle.erased.question: withheld
settle.erased.says: Once a record naming it in erases is held, every form of its target is erased.

admit.set.question: current
admit.set.says: A record is refused exactly when it isn't entitled to its prev, and that depends only on the set.

admit.no-cross.question: current
admit.no-cross.says: Every held record an admitted record's prev names shares a thing with it, and may be replaced by it.
admit.no-cross.scope: A prev naming a record the reader doesn't hold is admitted: the reader can't judge it. A writer refuses a prev naming a record it doesn't hold (prev-unknown); a reader that lacks it admits the record.

thing.local.question: current
thing.local.change: the records not about this thing, once records are settled and admitted
thing.local.scope: Admission and erasure can read records not about this thing, so this starts after them.

view.no-resurrection (things).question: withheld
view.no-resurrection (things).stays: the admitted records and each thing's heads by id
view.no-resurrection (things).scope: Every record comes back in the view's form; a record superseded in a thing is never current there.

where.complements.question: tests
where.complements.says: Where a test answers, not complements is; absent complements present. With a held safe whole value and a numeric bound, exactly one of at-least and below holds. Present times obey the corresponding time law.
where.complements.scope: On a payload the reader doesn't hold, a payload test answers unknown, and so does its complement.

where.typed.question: tests
where.typed.says: A test is accepted exactly when its operator and argument fit its field, and renders back as it was written.
where.typed.scope: Numeric arguments and bounds are safe-whole. Integral decimals and exponents normalize to integers before parsing.

where.fields.question: tests
where.fields.says: kind and observer read as their text; about, prev, under and erases as their members; emitted as its instant.

where.time.question: spelling
where.time.change: an accepted envelope time or test time, while keeping its parsed span
where.time.scope: An instant has one accepted spelling. Date claims can retain the same span with different qualifiers. A time in a payload remains text.

where.total.question: tests
where.total.says: A test answers for every record whose payload is here, and an envelope test for every record at all.

where.set.question: spelling
where.set.change: the order of a where map's tests

view.refines (where).question: withheld
view.refines (where).says: Under a view, a test and a where map keep their answer, or it becomes unknown.

spec.select.question: withheld
spec.select.stays: the set of records a spec's from takes
spec.select.scope: Each comes back in the view's form. A where test on a payload can still answer unknown under a view (view.refines).

spec.from-thing.question: tests
spec.from-thing.says: from's about takes exactly the records about the thing; a record about nothing is about its own id.

spec.set.question: arrival
spec.set.change: the order the records arrive in
spec.set.scope: Each id is handed over once (input.distinct).

spec.after-supersession.question: current
spec.after-supersession.says: A slot over heads returns only records that remain heads of at least one thing. Each returned record passes from and every test.
spec.after-supersession.scope: A record about several things can be superseded in one and still head another. Under a view, each thing keeps the same heads, and each head shows only what the view shows.

spec.parse.question: text
spec.parse.says: An accepted spec's parsed form parses back to itself, and the parser gives exactly the specs that fit.

batch.meaning.question: spelling
batch.meaning.says: An acyclic batch has at most one meaning. Any two satisfying assignments of ids to its labels agree.
batch.meaning.scope: Vectors check resolver answers across draft rotations. The uniqueness theorem does not prove resolver correctness.

batch.refuse.question: refused
batch.refuse.says: Duplicate labels, missing labels and cycles are refused. Drafts must pass write checks. Each prev target must be held and share a thing.

batch.refuse-order.question: refused
batch.refuse-order.change: the draft order and the order each stage finds its refusals in
batch.refuse-order.scope: Across the batch: shape, then labels, then writing, then prev-unknown, then prev-unrelated. Raw shape checks all envelope keys before any draft value, label or salt decode. The keys-only theorem permits arbitrary values and member reorderings. Writing's priority is proved from the refusal set. Stage order is by construction, pinned by raw-input rotations.

lens.escaping.question: text
lens.escaping.says: Any body survives rendering and parsing, backslashes and all.

lens.round-trip.question: text
lens.round-trip.says: Render, then parse, and you get back what you rendered.

lens.base-valid.question: text
lens.base-valid.says: A successful public edit establishes nonempty, distinct base ids.

lens.no-op.question: text
lens.no-op.says: A successful public edit of the unedited render gives no outcomes and keeps the base.

lens.put-get.question: text
lens.put-get.says: A successful public edit with the same ordered ids applies exactly. Rendering the applied result gives its normal form.

lens.apply-diff.question: text
lens.apply-diff.says: A successful public edit takes each known body from the parsed document and keeps absent base sections in base order.

lens.nothing-dropped.question: text
lens.nothing-dropped.says: Every section is unchanged, accepted or reported; every dropped one is reported.

lens.absence-not-edit.question: text
lens.absence-not-edit.change: the text by dropping a section
lens.absence-not-edit.scope: Absence is never an edit; the other sections' accepted edits still apply.

normal form.question: text
normal form.change: whether text that is already normal is normalized again

lens.refuse.question: refused
lens.refuse.says: The parser refuses malformed text, empty ids and repeated ids. The public entry also refuses invalid bases.
lens.refuse.scope: Refusals stay untyped. Mixed-invalid vectors check results, not base-before-parse order.

record.erasure.question: withheld
record.erasure.change: whether the payload's opening is kept

record.commit.question: withheld
record.commit.says: A record's own salt and payload open its commitment.

record.sets.question: spelling
record.sets.change: the order of, and repeats in, about, prev or erases

record.member-order.question: spelling
record.member-order.change: the order of an object's members

UTF-16 order.question: spelling
UTF-16 order.says: Any two distinct strings order one way, by UTF-16 code units.

record.refuse.question: refused
record.refuse.says: Writing refuses a bad envelope, an invalid salt length, a repeated member name, or a nonfinite or out-of-range number. Every number's magnitude must be at most 2<sup>53</sup> − 1, whole or not.

write.checked.question: refused
write.checked.says: write succeeds exactly when every check passes, and what it returns carries the proof.

write.member-order.question: spelling
write.member-order.change: the order of a written payload's members

occurred.span.question: spelling
occurred.span.says: Each accepted point gives its grammar-defined span, alone or open-ended. Two points form an interval when the second starts no earlier. Spans never end before their start.
occurred.span.scope: Which texts are points is the grammar itself, pinned by vectors, not proved.

occurred.qualifier.question: spelling
occurred.qualifier.change: a qualifier on a date, ?, ~ or %

occurred.moment.question: spelling
occurred.moment.says: A parsed moment contains whole seconds and a fraction without trailing zeros. List comparison equals exact decimal comparison.
occurred.moment.scope: The comparison theorem takes two stripped fractions and a scale at least as long as both. Accepted instant fractions already have canonical spelling.

occurred.order.question: current
occurred.order.says: Spans order by start, then end, an open end last, with no ties: any two stores that order by it agree.

occurred.refuse.question: refused
occurred.refuse.says: A text the reader doesn't accept is refused with occurred-not-span, never guessed at.

notTheorems.Written: a structure, not a theorem: what write returns, carrying the proof that every check passed

vectorTags.record.id: the id's definition, pinned byte for byte by the vectors; nothing to prove beyond computing it
vectorTags.record.sign: the signature's definition, checked against RFC 8032 values before any vector is written
vectorTags.record.canonical: the canonical bytes, RFC 8785, pinned by the vectors and the standard's own test data
vectorTags.record.emitted: emitted's grammar, which is its definition (instant?), pinned by the vectors

implementations.name: the model
implementations.what: lake exe gen computes protocol-vector answers. The theorem files separately prove the listed laws.

implementations.name: the Rust implementation
implementations.what: The Rust workspace checks all fixture families and external standards

demos.change: Deliver them in another order, the head's payload withheld
demos.done: Same heads, by id, for {n} orders the vector holds, the head's payload withheld in each. Max and unread are the model's answer too; they are not what this card compares. The vector's README says: “With consistent forms, these are the same heads as the full reader's.”

quote.text: With consistent forms, these are the same heads as the full reader's.

demos.note: The vector varies arrival order and withholds the head's payload in every variant. It holds no variant in which the reader holds every payload.

demos.change: Render it, then parse the text
Drop a section from the text
